title: Pullback of normalized lattice fibres and independence of charts
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Write $\mathscr A_E(Z)$ for the finite-stage standard heart, $J_Z$ for its continuous rational realization [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], and $\omega_{\bar z,E}$ for the normalized exact finite-dimensional geometric fibre [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness]. Its lattice prescription on an affine etale chart of a lisse stratum is $M_{\bar z}=\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar z}$ and $\omega_{\bar z,E}(F)=M_{\bar z}[1/\varpi_E]$, with a fractional lattice arrow $u/\varpi_E^a$ acting by $\varpi_E^{-a}\varprojlim_n u_n$.

For a morphism $g:Y\to X$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$, put $\bar x=g\bar y$. Use actual completed rational pullback and its heart restriction [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, lem-per-adic-stratified-pullback-texact]. There is a natural isomorphism $\alpha_{g,F}:\omega_{\bar y,E}(g^*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)$ with the following specified integral normalization. On any affine etale lattice chart $U\to S$ through a lift of $\bar x$ on a lisse stratum, let $N_\bullet$ be the normalized finite-free etale reduction tower of the lattice [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison]. At every level the tower map is the coefficient-linear inverse-image stalk comparison $c_{g,N_n}:(g^{-1}N_n)_{\bar y}\to(N_n)_{\bar x}$, sending the germ of a pulled section to its original germ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. The integral comparison is the inverse limit of these maps and $\alpha$ is its localization at $\varpi_E$. It computes the actual pulled lattice under the $J$ comparison with derived module inverse image on $Y\times_X S$. If the pulled chart is not affine as a scheme, this description holds on every affine open neighbourhood of the chosen lifted point in $U\times_X(Y\times_X S)$.

These maps commute with quotient transitions and all fractional lattice maps, and satisfy the identity and composite-pullback equations for the actual functor comparisons. On a common etale refinement a change of lattice is represented, using fully faithful raw lattice rationalization, by a fractional integral map. Conjugation by its normalized fibre map identifies the two computations of $\alpha$. The same identification holds on changing chart and adapted stratification. Equality of fractional representatives, meaning that a uniformizer power annihilates their cleared difference, gives identical rational fibre comparisons. Thus the comparison is independent of all these choices, with no flatness hypothesis on $g$ and no assertion that arbitrary pro-etale stalks commute with inverse limits.

proof.text: Obtain normalized fibres ω and the objectwise unit- and lattice-normalized isomorphisms p. This is only the objectwise construction, with neither naturality nor identity/composition coherence.

Apply the naturality theorem to each heart arrow. NatIso.ofComponents assembles p.component into a natural isomorphism α. Its hom components are definitionally those of p, so both normalization clauses transfer literally.
Apply the coherence theorem for p. Since α has literally the same components, its identity and composition equations are the required ones, with the underlying raw isomorphisms retained.

In the local-normalization clause replace the supplied PullLimit by HasLimit.isoOfNatIso of pullTowerIso. Its projection is HasLimit.isoOfNatIso_hom_π. Both comparisons have identical projections, hence their homs agree by limit.hom_ext, their isomorphisms agree by Iso.ext and their proof fields agree by proof irrelevance. Transport the local equation along this equality. Assemble all five fields of NormalizedPullback.
